title: Nebula Diagnostics onboarding kickoff & VPC intake
summary: Kickoff for onboarding Nebula Diagnostics onto Redwood Inference. Covered architecture choices (hosted vs private), VPC networking intake, security requirements (SOC 2, K-M-S integration), performance baseline needs for inference on clinical text, and pilot success criteria. Agreed next steps: security docs, pricing for dedicated pool, and schedule pilot load test week of 4/6.
topics: Deployment mode decision: hosted vs private VPC
action_items: Maya - send initial Dedicated pricing sheet and pilot agreement by 2026-03-27
Ethan - prepare a simple benchmark runbook and sample request payloads (due 2026-04-01)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:02
Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Ross (Redwood) / Dr. Lina Morales, Samir Desai, Jenna Ortiz, Ravi Nair (Nebula Diagnostics)

Summary (auto): quick kickoff to align on onboarding runway, security, and pilot plan.

00:00 - Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, and with me is Ethan our solutions engineer. Um, quick check — everyone can hear me?
00:08 - Dr. Lina (CTO): Yep, loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:12 - Maya: Great. So our agenda is short: intake for VPC/private deployment, security checklist, pilot scope and timelines, and then action items. If anything else please flag.
00:25 - Samir (Head of ML): Quick context — we're doing clinical note parsing and entity extraction, low latency matters but more important is throughput and cost predictability. We'll probably start with 10 rps bursty, then scale to a sustained 50 rps in phase 2.
00:47 - Ethan (Redwood SE): Got it. Do you have current latency SLOs you want to hit? 95th percentile, etc?
00:54 - Samir: Ideally P95 < 250ms for short prompts (~150 tokens). If we have to trade off, we'd prefer slightly higher latency if it halves cost — budget constraints.
01:10 - Maya: Makes sense — we often recommend Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or Private if you need VPC and full network isolation. Both support our caching and batching optimizations.
01:26 - Jenna (SRE): On security side we're SOC two compliant internally and will need Redwood's SOC2 report, audit logs, and K-M-S integration for key management. We also need RBAC tied into our SSO.
01:44 - Maya: Absolutely — we'll send SOC2 and our compliance pack. For KMS we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys; H-S-M integrations are on our roadmap but we do have enterprise hooks.
02:01 - Ravi (Product): On residency, all PII must remain in our region (us-east-1) until de-id pipeline completes. Is regional pinning available?
02:09 - Ethan: Yes, we can route requests to region-specific endpoints and we also support private deployments in your VPC. There might be some latency delta but routing preserves data locality.
02:25 - Dr. Lina: For the VPC setup, what do you need from us for the network intake?
02:30 - Ethan: We'll need CIDR blocks, a list of allowed egress destinations, and firewall policy — plus a jump host for initial testing. Also a temporary service account for API keys scoped to the pilot.
02:44 - Jenna: Ok, we'll extract the VPC CIDR and egress list, and share contact for networking.
02:50 - Samir: Regarding models — do you host open models only or also offer Redwood-curated variants? We want to avoid massive ops overhead for model upgrades.
02:59 - Maya: We have a model catalog — open models and Redwood-verified builds. You can pin a model version for the pilot; we also offer quantized variants for cost savings.
03:12 - Samir: Quantization detail — do you do int8? Any regression monitoring?
03:16 - Ethan: Yes, we support quantization and have a quality monitoring hook — you can run evals against your prompt set and get regression alerts. Slight mis-recog: we call it quality watch in the console.
03:31 - Dr. Lina: On observability: we need per-request tracing + token-level cost breakdowns for our finance team.
03:37 - Maya: That's in Redwood Console: token breakdown, route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll show you a quick demo in the next call.
03:45 - Ravi: One concern — vendor lock in. If we start with Dedicated, how portable are prompts and model versions if we later move on-prem?
03:54 - Ethan: Portability is a focus — same API surface across hosted, Dedicated, and Private. You can pin and export model configs; some infra migration steps will be required but we try to avoid app-level changes.
04:08 - Samir: Ok good. For pilot— what success criteria should we follow?
04:12 - Maya: Typical pilot success is: functional parity with your current infra, latency within agreed SLO (P95 < 300ms for pilot), and cost baseline within estimate. Also security acceptance — SOC2 and KMS checks passed.
04:26 - Dr. Lina: Timeline? We need pilot in April (end-to-end) to feed Q2 roadmap.
04:32 - Maya: We proposed the load test week of 2026-04-06 in the invite. If we get the VPC details and prompts by the end of March we can prepare a benchmark and start smoke tests early April.
04:46 - Jenna: We'll prioritize the network details.
04:49 - Ethan: I'll draft a simple benchmark runbook: sample payloads, keys, expected metrics. We'll also run an initial hosted smoke run to baseline before any VPC connectivity is done.
05:02 - Samir: Any compliance red flags — HIPAA? We're not fully HIPAA yet but clinical domain, do you have an approach?
05:09 - Maya: We have private deployment options designed for regulated workloads; for HIPAA we typically recommend Private or Dedicated with BAAs — we'll include BAA guidance in the pack.
05:20 - Ravi: For cost modelling, can you provide an estimate for Dedicated pool sizing for sustained 50 rps?
05:27 - Ethan: We'll produce a rough sizing estimate; depends on model choice (quantized vs fp16) and sequence length. I'll include a couple of scenarios in the pricing sheet.
05:38 - Maya: Quick recap: Redwood sends compliance pack (SOC2, BAA guidance), Dedicated pricing and pilot agreement; SE runs benchmark runbook and shares initial hosted baseline; Nebula provides VPC CIDR, egress, and prompt set. Agreed pilot week of 4/6 pending artifacts.
05:58 - Dr. Lina: Sounds good. Any blockers from your side?
06:02 - Maya: None, we'll get docs out by Friday. Thanks everyone.
06:06 - Jenna: Thanks all.
06:09 - Ethan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the links and runbook.
06:13 - Meeting ends.
